title: Infection: Avoid the Unhappy and Unlucky
summary: Avoid associating with chronically unstable and negative individuals who bring misfortune upon themselves through their own actions. These infectors often possess a highly charismatic and persuasive charm, but trying to help or save them will only result in your own downfall and reputational ruin. Instead, quarantine yourself from negative influencers and surround yourself with wise, successful, and positive people to inherit their beneficial qualities.
example: Lola Montez used her charm to lure and financially ruin multiple men, including King Ludwig of Bavaria, who lost his reputation and throne by refusing to distance himself from her self-inflicted misery.
Cassius, driven by envy and dissatisfaction, infected Brutus with his negativity, leading Brutus to turn against Caesar and face his own downfall.
Napoleon purposely kept the witty and well-mannered Talleyrand close to absorb his superior qualities and improve himself.
reversal: There is no reversal to this law; absolutely nothing good comes from keeping bad company, and you must never die for someone else's misery.
